mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over three months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where HOUST increased consistently over the previous three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% over two months signals a contraction in supply, which can lead to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO decreased by more than 1% over the previous two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the consumer price index increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with high interest rates
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2% in a month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where both conditions are met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures over three months signals a strengthening consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS increased consistently over the previous three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and the GDP increases by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter, it signals accommodative monetary policy with strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: economic expansion with low interest rates
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where both conditions are met.
